blocks.html: None of this is medical advice, and none of it is about arguing with your doctor. It's about walking in with the information already in a form somebody can read — which is most of what makes a short appointment go well.

blocks.imageDescription: notebook pen wooden table window light

blocks.html: Most people arrive with symptoms. Far fewer arrive with dates. I've been tired for a while and I've woken at 3am roughly four nights a week since October are the same information, and they produce completely different conversations.

items: Three weeks of dated notes is already enough to be worth bringing
Numbers land where adverbs don't — four nights a week, not often
A record is harder to wave off than a description

blocks.html: You don't need all of this. Anything from the list beats arriving with none of it.

items: Dated notes on what changed and when it started
How often it happens, in numbers rather than adverbs
Anything that makes it better or worse
What you've already tried, and what happened
The one outcome you want from this appointment
Something to write on — you won't remember it afterwards

blocks.html: It might be. It might also be the first answer rather than the final one. Either way, the useful move is a question rather than a disagreement.

items: Ask the follow-up: if it isn't perimenopause, what else would explain this pattern?
Ask what would need to be true for it to be worth investigating
Ask what to watch for, and when to come back
Bring the record — written dates are harder to wave off
Ask for the reasoning to be written in your notes

blocks.text: 4. Write it down before you get to the car

blocks.html: The five minutes straight after the appointment are the ones you'll wish you had back. Capture it while it's still exact.

items: What was said, in their words rather than your summary
Anything ruled out, and the reason given
What was agreed, and who does it next
What you were told to watch for
The question you didn't get to ask

blocks.html: This page is about preparing for an appointment. It isn't medical advice, it isn't a diagnosis, and it doesn't replace talking to a clinician who knows your history.
